eyebrow: Three flags worth setting on every script

steps.label: set -e
steps.sub: exit immediately if any command fails

steps.label: set -u
steps.sub: error on an unset (likely mistyped) variable

steps.label: set -x
steps.sub: trace every command as it runs, for debugging

eyebrow: A failure that would otherwise hide
code:
$ grep "ERROR" /var/log/nonexistent.log | wc -l
grep: /var/log/nonexistent.log: No such file or directory
0

$ set -o pipefail
$ echo $?
1
caption: pipefail makes the pipeline's status reflect the first command that failed

eyebrow: Clean up no matter how the script ends
code:
#!/bin/bash
tmpfile=$(mktemp)
trap 'rm -f "$tmpfile"' EXIT

echo "Working in $tmpfile"
# ...script logic that might fail anywhere...
caption: trap ... EXIT runs cleanup on normal exit, an error, or Ctrl-C

eyebrow: Trace exactly what a script is doing
code:
$ bash -x ./deploy.sh
+ environment=production
+ echo 'Deploying to production'
Deploying to production
caption: bash -x prints each command, with values substituted, before it runs
